summary: Anthropic launched Claude Science, a beta AI workbench app that lets scientists run multi-agent Claude-based research workflows integrated with common scientific databases, tools and on-demand compute.

mechanisms.reason: The product is built around a coordinating agent that spawns and coordinates specialist sub-agents to execute multi-step scientific work, an example of agent-executed task delegation.
mechanisms.quote: Users interact with a generalist coordinating agent with access to over 60 curated skills and connectors pre-configured for genomics, single-cell, proteomics, structural biology, cheminformatics, and more. These agents can spin up others and engage with specialist agents created by users.

mechanisms.reason: Agents maintain long-lived sessions that hold large dataset context in memory across many steps rather than reloading it, increasing memory footprint per session.
mechanisms.quote: Because its agents work inside a running session that holds context in memory, even massive datasets only need to be loaded once.

practices.reason: The actor-critic reviewer-agent pattern for checking generated content is a concrete multi-agent design an engineering team could adapt for their own pipelines.
practices.quote: A key component of the workflow, enabled by Claude Science, is the use of actor-critic pairs: one agent creates content while a separate reviewer agent evaluates it for accuracy and citation fidelity.

practices.reason: A reviewer agent that automatically flags incorrect citations, untraceable numbers and mismatched figures is a transferable monitoring/validation technique for trusting agent outputs.
practices.quote: As the pipeline runs, a reviewer agent inspects the outputs, flagging incorrect citations, untraceable numbers, and figures that don’t match their underlying code, and self-correcting as it goes.
